answer: SybilLimit-style random-walk sampling makes the trust graph itself the gate: each agent grows short random routes, and two peers accept one another only when their routes intersect. Honest agents form a fast-mixing graph, while clones hang off a thin cut of hard-won attack edges, an ivory tower no verifier's walk reaches. Minting N seats is no fable of free keys, it costs N genuine vouched social edges, each a pearl an honest peer will not surrender cheaply.
